text: keep 20% samples testing. data hold repeated samples, splits keep spectra sample together: model partial least squares (PLS) regression, mixOmics engine parsnip, number components tuned. compare three recipes: baseline correction followed SNV, carbon internal standard, carbon standard wavelet compression:  three recipes give similar errors number components tuned: PLS finds potassium information , normalization matters less multivariate model single line. carbon + wavelet recipe best small margin. refit whole training set best number components, evaluate test samples: test error, 0.32% K, somewhat larger cross-validated one (0.26%): 74 test spectra, uncertain.  fitted workflow applies every step, values estimated training data, new spectra: predict(extract_workflow(final), new_data). prepped recipe also shows step estimated, tidy(). next vignette, vignette("calibration"), builds univariate calibration curves computes figures merit kinds models.
code: set.seed(1) split <- group_initial_split(forageLIBS, group = Sample, prop = 0.8) training_set <- training(split) folds <- group_vfold_cv(training_set, group = Sample, v = 5) baseline_step <- \(r) step_baseline(r, all_predictors(), lambda = 1e5, options = list(max.iter = 20)) carbon_step <- \(r) step_line_ratio(r, all_predictors(), reference = 247.856, window = 0.15)  recipes <- list(   SNV = base |> baseline_step() |> step_snv(all_predictors()),   carbon = base |> baseline_step() |> carbon_step(),   `carbon + wavelet` = base |> baseline_step() |> carbon_step() |>     step_wavelet(all_predictors(), level = 3) )  # mixOmics scales every predictor by default; scale = FALSE only centers pls_model <- pls(num_comp = tune()) |>   set_mode("regression") |>   set_engine("mixOmics", scale = FALSE) tuned <- map(recipes, \(rec) {   tune_grid(workflow(rec, pls_model), resamples = folds,             grid = tibble(num_comp = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15)),             metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq)) })  map(tuned, \(res) show_best(res, metric = "rmse", n = 1)) |>   bind_rows(.id = "recipe") |>   select(recipe, num_comp, rmse = mean, std_err) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   recipe           num_comp  rmse std_err #>   <chr>               <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 SNV                     8 0.262  0.0187 #> 2 carbon                 10 0.257  0.0183 #> 3 carbon + wavelet       12 0.256  0.0224 map(tuned, collect_metrics) |>   bind_rows(.id = "recipe") |>   filter(.metric == "rmse") |>   ggplot(aes(num_comp, mean, colour = recipe)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   labs(x = "PLS components", y = "Cross-validated RMSE (% K)", colour = NULL) +   theme_bw() final <- workflow(recipes[[best_recipe]], pls_model) |>   finalize_workflow(select_best(tuned[[best_recipe]], metric = "rmse")) |>   last_fit(split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq)) collect_metrics(final) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       0.321 pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.694 pre0_mod0_post0 collect_predictions(final) |>   ggplot(aes(K, .pred)) +   geom_abline(colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +   geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +   coord_equal() +   labs(x = "Laboratory K (%)", y = "Predicted K (%)") +   theme_bw()

text: function applies Eilers' method based Whittaker filter. algorithm estimates baseline curve minimizing asymmetric least squares criterion, allows different weights positive negative residuals. resulting baseline curve subtracted input data, providing baseline-corrected version. penalized system pentadiagonal solved C++ banded Cholesky decomposition, cost grows linearly number spectral channels. code: data(forageLIBS) spectrum <- forageLIBS[1, -(1:14)] wl <- as.numeric(names(spectrum)) in_region <- wl > 240 & wl < 300 region <- spectrum[in_region] res <- baseline_als(region, lambda = 1e6) oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) # the spectrum and its fitted baseline plot(wl[in_region], unlist(region), type = "l", col = "grey40", ylim = c(800, 3000),      xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Counts", main = "Spectrum and baseline") lines(wl[in_region], unlist(res$background), col = "red") # the corrected spectrum: the background is now around zero plot(wl[in_region], unlist(res$correction), type = "l", col = "grey40",      ylim = c(-200, 2000), xlab = "Wavelength (nm)", ylab = "Counts",      main = "Corrected spectrum") abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)  par(oldpar)

text: lines data frame one row per line columns intensity (integrated line intensity), wavelength (nm), Aki (transition probability, s\(^{-1}\)), gk (upper-level degeneracy) Ek (upper-level energy, eV). units units intensity: "energy" (default; radiance energy-calibrated counts) "photons" (photon counts).

text: LTE, integrated intensity line emitted upper level energy \(E_k\) degeneracy \(g_k\), transition probability \(A_{ki}\) wavelength \(\lambda\), satisfies $$\ln\frac{\lambda}{g_k A_{ki}} = -\frac{E_k}{k_B T} + C$$ intensities energy units, \(\ln(/ g_k A_{ki})\) photon counts (units = "photons"). least-squares line points gives temperature slope, \(T = -1/(k_B\,\mathrm{slope})\), standard error slope. intensities must corrected spectral response instrument, lines must optically thin (see self_absorption()). wide range upper-level energies gives precise temperature. code: data(forageLIBS) mean_spectrum <- colMeans(forageLIBS[-(1:14)]) # calcium and magnesium lines, with their atomic data from the NIST database atomic <- data.frame(   species = c("Ca I", "Ca I", "Ca I", "Ca II", "Ca II", "Mg I", "Mg I", "Mg I", "Mg II", "Mg II"),   wavelength = c(428.301, 430.253, 445.478, 315.887, 317.933,                  516.732, 517.268, 518.360, 279.078, 279.800),   Aki = c(4.34e7, 1.36e8, 8.70e7, 3.10e8, 3.60e8, 1.13e7, 3.37e7, 5.61e7, 4.01e8, 4.79e8),   gk = c(5, 5, 7, 4, 6, 3, 3, 3, 4, 6),   Ek = c(4.780, 4.780, 4.681, 7.047, 7.050, 5.108, 5.108, 5.108, 8.864, 8.864) ) # partition functions, interpolated from a table (see partition_function()) partition <- function(species, temperature) {   grid <- c(6000, 8000, 10000, 12000)   table <- rbind(`Ca I` = c(1.407, 2.401, 4.499, 8.356), `Ca II` = c(2.389, 2.917, 3.560, 4.262),                  `Mg I` = c(1.049, 1.207, 1.597, 2.463), `Mg II` = c(2.001, 2.010, 2.036, 2.087))   vapply(species, function(s) exp(stats::approx(grid, log(table[s, ]), xout = temperature)$y),          numeric(1)) } fit <- cf_libs(line_intensities(mean_spectrum, atomic, baseline = TRUE),                electron_density = 1.9e17, partition = partition,                ionization_energy = c(Ca = 6.113, Mg = 7.646)) fit #> Calibration-free LIBS (10 lines, 4 species; Saha-Boltzmann plots) #>  #> Temperature:  8946 +/- 290 K #> Ne:           1.9e+17 cm-3 #> Normalization: closure #>  #>  element atomic_fraction mass_fraction stages #>  Ca      0.4512          0.5755        I, II  #>  Mg      0.5488          0.4245        I, II  plot_boltzmann(fit)

title: Direct Orthogonal Signal Correction — direct_osc
text: Different Orthogonal Signal Correction (OSC) algorithm, Wold et al. (1998), DOSC algorithm non-iterative: \(\textbf{Y}\) projected onto column space \(\textbf{X}\): \(\hat{\textbf{Y}} = \textbf{XX}^{+}\textbf{Y}\). \(\textbf{X}\) orthogonalized respect \(\hat{\textbf{Y}}\): \(\textbf{Z} = \textbf{X} - \hat{\textbf{Y}}\hat{\textbf{Y}}^{+}\textbf{X}\). PCA \(\textbf{Z}\) gives orthogonal scores \(\textbf{T}\). weights \(\textbf{W} = \textbf{X}^{+}\textbf{T}\) express scores linear combination \(\textbf{X}\), loadings \(\textbf{P} = \textbf{X}^T\textbf{T}(\textbf{T}^T\textbf{T})^{-1}\), corrected matrix \(\textbf{X} - \textbf{TP}^T\). New data corrected \(\textbf{X}_{new} - \textbf{X}_{new}\textbf{WP}^T\) applying returned center scale.

title: External Parameter Orthogonalization — epo
text: object class specproc_epo (list), predict() applies new spectra, four components: correction: orthogonalized matrix, representing signal interest. clutter: clutter part x, \(\textbf{XVV}^T\). loadings: singular vectors \(\textbf{V}\) used orthogonalization. singular_values: corresponding singular values clutter matrix.

title: External Parameter Orthogonalization — epo
text: EPO algorithm works detecting dominant directions (right singular vectors) clutter matrix \(\textbf{D}\) describe external variations, e.g. differences spectra samples measured different temperatures moisture levels. projects spectral matrix onto subspace orthogonal variations, effectively removing unwanted perturbations extracting signal interest. Let \(\textbf{X}\) spectral matrix. EPO algorithm aims split \(\textbf{X}\) : $$\textbf{X} = \textbf{XP} + \textbf{XQ} + \textbf{R}$$ \(\textbf{P}\) \(\textbf{Q}\) , respectively, projection matrices \(\textbf{X}\) onto useful perturbation (clutter) subspaces. \(\textbf{R}\) residual matrix. \(\textbf{V}\) first ncomp right singular vectors \(\textbf{D}\), \(\textbf{Q} = \textbf{VV}^T\) corrected matrix \(\textbf{X} - \textbf{XVV}^T\). singular value decomposition computed C++ (Eigen), \(p \times p\) projection matrix never formed explicitly.

title: Net Analyte Signal and Figures of Merit — nas
text: net analyte signal part spectrum unique analyte, .e. orthogonal spectral contributions constituents (interferents). inverse calibration model \(\hat{y} = \bar{y} + (\textbf{x} - \bar{\textbf{x}})^T\textbf{b}\) \(\) latent variables, interferent space spanned calibration spectra reconstructed model, part explained \(\hat{\textbf{y}}\) removed. regression vector \(\textbf{b}\) orthogonal space, NAS space within model one-dimensional spanned \(\textbf{b}\) (Faber, 1998; Bro Andersen, 2003). NAS vector sample \(\) therefore $$\textbf{r}_i^* = \frac{(\textbf{x}_i - \bar{\textbf{x}})^T\textbf{b}}{\|\textbf{b}\|^2}\,\textbf{b}$$ signed length, scalar NAS, $$\mathrm{NAS}_i = \frac{(\textbf{x}_i - \bar{\textbf{x}})^T\textbf{b}}{\|\textbf{b}\|} = \frac{\hat{y}_i - \bar{y}}{\|\textbf{b}\|}$$ figures merit follow Olivieri et al. (2006): Sensitivity, \(\mathrm{SEN} = 1 / \|\textbf{b}\|\): NAS produced unit change concentration, signal units per concentration unit. Selectivity sample \(\), \(\mathrm{SEL}_i = |\mathrm{NAS}_i| / \|\textbf{x}_i - \bar{\textbf{x}}\|\): fraction (centered) signal used prediction, 0 1. standard deviation instrumental noise \(\sigma_x\) (noise): analytical sensitivity \(\gamma = \mathrm{SEN} / \sigma_x\), whose inverse smallest concentration difference can distinguished; limit detection \(\mathrm{LOD} = 3.3\,\sigma_x / \mathrm{SEN}\); limit quantification \(\mathrm{LOQ} = 10\,\sigma_x / \mathrm{SEN}\); signal--noise ratio sample, \(\mathrm{NAS}_i / \sigma_x\). LOD LOQ account instrumental noise , uncertainty calibration model reference values, lower bounds. noise level must estimated independently, example standard deviation differences repeated spectra sample divided \(\sqrt{2}\), units (preprocessing) x. quantities depend number latent variables ncomp, chosen validation beforehand. specProc 0.4.0, nas() returned spectra filtered direct orthogonalization; correction available direct_orthogonal().

title: Spectra Normalization — normalize
text: normalization methods: Normalization background: Spectra divided intensity background emission. Note recommended detector dark current subtracted prior normalization. Normalization total area: spectrum divided total area spectrum whole spectral range. detector dark current must subtracted prior normalization. total area calculated sum intensity levels. L1 normalization ("l1"): spectrum divided sum absolute values intensities. equals total area non-negative spectra, also suits derivative spectra, whose values change sign. L2 (vector) normalization ("l2"): spectrum divided Euclidean norm, sum squares 1. Unlike SNV, spectrum centered. Maximum normalization ("max"): spectrum divided largest absolute intensity, strongest feature 1 (-1). Normalization internal standard: peak intensity (area) emission line related analyte divided peak intensity (area) selected emission line related internal standard. internal standard concentration assumed constant known.

text: x1 matrix data frame containing spectra acquired standard (master) instrument. x2 matrix data frame containing spectra samples acquired instrument standardized (slave). win integer specifying half size moving window used PLSR. larger value may improve transfer increase computational time. Default 5. ncomp integer specifying number components used PLSR. Typically, small number (e.g., 2-5) sufficient. title: Piecewise Direct Standardization — pds

Spectra measured slave instrument standardized $$\textbf{X}_{2,std} = \textbf{X}_2 \textbf{F} + \textbf{1}\textbf{b}_0^T$$ alpha > 0, global PLSR model mapping whole slave spectrum whole master spectrum also fitted, transfer matrix intercept \((1 - \alpha)\) times local ones plus \(\alpha\) times global ones.

code: # robust PCA of the forage spectra, with the Hotelling's T-squared limit if (rlang::is_installed("HotellingEllipse", version = "1.3.0")) {   data(forageLIBS)   # the 380-430 nm window (Ca II H and K lines)   wl <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(names(forageLIBS)))   set.seed(1)   forageLIBS[which(wl > 380 & wl < 430)] |>     center() |>     robpca(k = 2) |>     plot_embedding(hotelling = "all", flag = FALSE, label = TRUE) }   # UMAP map of the iris flowers, from embed::step_umap(): no lines through # the origin, whose position means nothing on such a map if (rlang::is_installed(c("recipes", "embed"))) {   set.seed(1)   umap <- recipes::recipe(Species ~ ., data = iris) |>     recipes::step_normalize(recipes::all_predictors()) |>     embed::step_umap(recipes::all_predictors(), neighbors = 15) |>     recipes::prep() |>     recipes::bake(new_data = NULL)   plot_embedding(umap, colour = Species, title = "UMAP of the iris flowers") }

title: Projected Orthogonal Signal Correction — projected_osc
text: POSC obtains OPLS-filtered data directly ordinary (non-orthogonalized) PLS1 model (Kemsley Tapp, 2009): PLS1 model ncomp + 1 components fitted, giving score matrix \(\textbf{T}\) fitted response \(\hat{\textbf{y}}\). part score space orthogonal \(\hat{\textbf{y}}\), \(\textbf{T} - \hat{\textbf{y}}(\hat{\textbf{y}}^T\hat{\textbf{y}})^{-1}\hat{\textbf{y}}^T\textbf{T}\), spans ncomp orthogonal components scores \(\textbf{T}_o\). orthogonal loadings \(\textbf{P}_o = \textbf{X}^T\textbf{T}_o(\textbf{T}_o^T\textbf{T}_o)^{-1}\) filtered data \(\textbf{X} - \textbf{T}_o\textbf{P}_o^T\). filtered data identical obtained OPLS model one predictive ncomp orthogonal components (opls() ncomp).

title: Projected Orthogonal Signal Correction — projected_osc

text: Pseudo-Voigt function given : $$y = y_0 + \cdot [ \eta \cdot L(x, x_c, w_L) + (1 - \eta) \cdot G(x, x_c, w_G)]$$ : \(\) peak area \(y_0\) baseline offset \(G(x, x_c, w_G)\) Gaussian component center \(x_c\) full width half maximum \(w_G\) \(L(x, x_c, w_L)\) Lorentzian component center \(x_c\) full width half maximum \(w_L\) \(\eta\) mixing parameter, \(0 \leq \eta \leq 1\). mixing parameter \(\eta\) allows pseudo-Voigt function describe wide range line shapes, pure Gaussian (\(\eta = 0\)) pure Lorentzian (\(\eta = 1\)), various intermediate shapes . \(G\) \(L\) unit area, \(\) area peak. eta given, Thompson-Cox-Hastings approximation Voigt profile used (Ida et al. 2000): components share total FWHM $$f = (w_G^5 + 2.69269 w_G^4 w_L + 2.42843 w_G^3 w_L^2 + 4.47163 w_G^2 w_L^3 + 0.07842 w_G w_L^4 + w_L^5)^{1/5}$$ mixing parameter $$\eta = 1.36603 (w_L/f) - 0.47719 (w_L/f)^2 + 0.11116 (w_L/f)^3$$ comparison, Olivero Longbothum (1977) approximation, subsequent refinements (Belafhal 2000; Zdunkowski et al. 2007), estimate FWHM Voigt line \(w_V = \frac{1}{2} [c_1 w_L + \sqrt{c_2 w_L^2 + 4 w_G^2}]\) \(c_1 = 1.0692\), \(c_2 = 0.86639\) (accuracy 0.02%).

title: Quantile Tail Weight Measure — quantile_weight
text: quantile weights, comprising left quantile weight (LQW) right quantile weight (RQW), robust measures tail weight probability distributions. breakdown value 12.5%, meaning resistant influence 12.5% outliers contaminated data. concept quantile weights derived quartile skewness, introduced D.V. Hinkley 1975. Quartile skewness measures skewness asymmetry distribution comparing differences quartiles, robust measures location scale. Specifically, quantile weights obtained applying quartile skewness either left half right half probability mass, divided median univariate distribution (Brys et al. 2006): $$LQW(p) = -\frac{Q((1-p)/2) + Q(p/2) - 2Q(0.25)}{Q((1-p)/2) - Q(p/2)}$$ $$RQW(q) = \frac{Q((1+q)/2) + Q(1-q/2) - 2Q(0.75)}{Q((1+q)/2) - Q(1-q/2)}$$ \(Q\) quantile function data. defaults \(p = 0.125\) \(q = 0.875\) give breakdown value 12.5%. Interpretation Quantile Weights: normal distribution, LQW = RQW = 0.2 (approximately). Larger values indicate heavier tails normal distribution, smaller values lighter tails.

what: specProc: Preprocessing Tools for Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy — specProc-package
title: specProc: Preprocessing Tools for Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy — specProc-package
text: Tools exploring, preprocessing modeling spectroscopic data, developed laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) also applicable techniques Raman, infrared, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy. Covers workflow raw spectra calibrated results: peak finding fitting, wavelength calibration, baseline correction, normalization scaling, orthogonal signal correction including orthogonal partial least squares (OPLS; Trygg Wold (2002) doi:10.1002/cem.695 ), calibration transfer, calibration curves figures merit, plasma diagnostics (Boltzmann Saha-Boltzmann plots, Stark broadening). Includes robust tools outlier detection exploration: robust principal component analysis (Hubert, Rousseeuw Vanden Branden (2005) doi:10.1198/004017004000000563 ), detection deviating cells (Rousseeuw Van den Bossche (2018) doi:10.1080/00401706.2017.1340909 ), PCA cellwise outliers missing values (MacroPCA; Hubert, Rousseeuw Van den Bossche (2019) doi:10.1080/00401706.2018.1562989 ), robust transformations central normality (Raymaekers Rousseeuw (2021) doi:10.1007/s10994-021-05960-5 ), self-organizing maps (Kohonen (1982) doi:10.1007/BF00337288 ). Preprocessing steps also available 'recipes' steps 'tidymodels' workflows. Computationally intensive steps implemented 'C++' via 'Rcpp' 'RcppEigen'.

text: num_comp joint_comp can tuned tune::tune() recipe single outcome. default ranges dials::num_comp() values 1 4 1 3; joint_comp exceed number outcomes. tune::tune_grid() support several outcomes. Instead, create one workflow per outcome workflowsets package, tune workflowsets::workflow_map("tune_grid", ...). recipe single outcome, model, filter can still estimated outcomes: give others role ("reference" ), needed bake new data, select outcome. outcome gets number filter model components:   Select outcomes role (all_outcomes(), has_role()) rather all_of(outcomes), refers variable outside recipe. filter outcome , drop outcomes recipe instead; step equivalent step_opls(). Read results outcome outcome: workflowsets::rank_results() rank workflows different outcomes, whose RMSE different units.
code: outcomes <- c("K", "Ca", "Mg") recipes <- purrr::map(outcomes, \(y) {   recipe(reformulate(".", response = y), data = spectra) |>     update_role(all_of(setdiff(outcomes, y)), new_role = "reference") |>     update_role_requirements("reference", bake = FALSE) |>     step_o2pls(all_predictors(), outcome = c(all_outcomes(), has_role("reference")),                num_comp = tune("filter"), joint_comp = length(outcomes)) }) |>   purrr::set_names(outcomes) model <- parsnip::pls(num_comp = tune()) |>   set_mode("regression") |>   set_engine("mixOmics", scale = FALSE)  wf_set <- workflow_set(preproc = recipes, models = list(pls = model)) res <- workflow_map(wf_set, "tune_grid", resamples = vfold_cv(spectra, v = 5),                     grid = 10, metrics = metric_set(rmse), seed = 1)  # best settings and final model of each outcome fits <- purrr::map(purrr::set_names(res$wflow_id), \(id) {   best <- select_best(extract_workflow_set_result(res, id), metric = "rmse")   extract_workflow(res, id) |>     finalize_workflow(best) |>     fit(data = spectra) }) purrr::map(fits, \(f) predict(f, new_data = new_spectra))

Ignored type = "r". type character string specifying function called (d density, p cumulative distribution, q quantile, r random number generation). location location parameter TGH distribution. scale scale parameter TGH distribution. g skewness parameter TGH distribution. h kurtosis parameter TGH distribution. log TRUE, log-density returned density function. title: Tukey g-and-h Parametric Distribution — tukey_gh
text: Tukey g--h distribution, introduced John W. Tukey 1977, defined two transformation functions, g h, applied standard normal distribution. g transformation controls skewness distribution, h transformation controls kurtosis (heaviness tails). TGH distribution given : $$T_{g,h}(Z) = \frac{1}{g} (e^{g Z} -1) e^{\frac{1}{2} h Z^2}$$ \(Z\) random variable standard normal distribution. parameters \(g\) \(h\) stand bias elongation tails, respectively, Tukey’s \(g\)--\(h\) distribution.

Summarizing shape numerically: g--h distributions. : Hoaglin, D.C., Mosteller, F., Tukey, J.W., (eds), Data Analysis Tables, Trends, Shapes. New York:Wiley.

title: Voigt Function — voigt_profile
text: x numeric vector representing independent variable (e.g., wavelength). y0 numeric value specifying baseline offset. xc numeric value representing center peak. wG non-negative numeric value specifying Gaussian full width half maximum (FWHM). wL non-negative numeric value specifying Lorentzian FWHM. numeric value representing peak area.

title: Voigt Function — voigt_profile
text: Voigt function defined : $$y = y_0 + \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} G(t; w_G)\, L(x - x_c - t; w_L)\, dt = y_0 + \frac{\mathrm{Re}[w(z)]}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}, \quad z = \frac{x - x_c + \gamma}{\sigma\sqrt{2}}$$ \(w(z) = e^{-z^2}\mathrm{erfc}(-iz)\) Faddeeva function, \(\sigma = w_G / (2\sqrt{2\ln 2})\) standard deviation Gaussian component \(\gamma = w_L / 2\) half width half maximum Lorentzian component. components unit area, \(\) area line. Faddeeva function evaluated C++ Weideman's (1994) rational approximation using 32 terms. relative error \(10^{-10}\) range widths met emission spectroscopy. width zero gives pure Gaussian pure Lorentzian profile. See pseudo_voigt_profile() faster pseudo-Voigt approximation.

text: y-Gradient GLSW alternative method GLSW, continuous \(\textbf{y}\)-variable used develop pseudo-groupings samples \(\textbf{X}\) comparing differences corresponding \(\textbf{y}\) values. referred "gradient method" utilizes gradient sorted \(\textbf{X}\)- \(\textbf{y}\)-blocks calculate covariance matrix. samples sorted increasing \(\textbf{y}\), first derivatives \(\textbf{X}\) \(\textbf{y}\) along sample axis computed Savitzky-Golay filter. text: cf_libs(): calibration-free LIBS quantification (Ciucci et al., 1999). temperature estimated common slope parallel Boltzmann plots (one per species) , electron density known, Saha-Boltzmann plots (one per element, much precise). densities follow intercepts partition functions, ionization stages observed Saha equation. composition (atomic mass fractions) normalized closure known concentration one element. plot_boltzmann() draws plots fit. plasma diagnostics vignette applies forage samples compares laboratory values. nist_levels() retrieves energy levels NIST Atomic Spectra Database, partition_function() computes partition functions , optionally truncated maximum energy (lowered ionization energy). reject_shots() flags outlying laser shots sample (total intensity, correlation distance median spectrum, robust z-scores), averaged average(). line_intensities() measures area (height, Voigt-fitted area) emission lines spectra, searching peak near tabulated wavelength, signal--noise ratio saturation check. keeps columns table lines, result feeds boltzmann_plot(), cf_libs() calibration_curve(). step_line_intensities() recipe. correct_self_absorption() corrects line intensities self-absorption internal reference method Sun Yu (2009), temperature given estimated Saha-Boltzmann plot. calibration_curve() fits univariate (linear quadratic, optionally weighted) calibration curves, sensitivity, LOD LOQ, Mandel’s lack--fit tests linearity, inverse prediction concentrations confidence intervals (predict()) plot_calibration(). New recipe steps: step_reject_shots() removes outlying shots training data (skipped new data), step_line_ratio() normalizes spectrum area height reference line (internal standard). line_finder(): Shiny app identify emission lines LIBS spectra. Elements selected periodic table, strongest lines ionization stages, NIST Atomic Spectra Database, overlaid spectrum interactive plotly graph (one color per stage), controls temperature, wavelength range, number lines, wavelength shift spectrum (mean, group mean single spectrum). Fetched lines can saved reloaded offline use. libs_lines() lists lines selected species expected strongest plasma given temperature (relative intensities LTE), plot_lines() overlays spectrum (plotly ggplot2).

title: specProc 0.2.0
text: release fixes large number bugs every exported function now runs returns numerically correct results. adds test suite (400+ expectations), several results checked independent reference implementations.

title: specProc 0.2.0
text: Functions renamed consistent snake_case scheme. old names still work give deprecation warning (see ?"specProc-deprecated"): whittaker() -> baseline_als(), lorentzian() -> lorentzian_profile(), pseudo_voigt() -> pseudo_voigt_profile(), peakfit() -> peak_fit(), multipeakfit() -> multipeak_fit(), plotfit() -> plot_fit(), plotSpec() -> plot_spectra(), outlierplot() -> plot_outliers(), directOutlyingness() -> directional_outlyingness(), iqrMethod() -> iqr_outliers(), robustBCYJ() -> robust_bcyj(), rousseeuwCroux() -> rousseeuw_croux(), summaryStats() -> summary_stats(), tukeyGH() -> tukey_gh(), yGradientglsw() -> y_gradient_glsw(), pareto() -> pareto_scale(). gaussian() renamed gaussian_profile() without alias, exporting gaussian() masked stats::gaussian(), breaks glm(family = gaussian) specProc loaded. baseline_arpls(), baseline_lsp() whittaker() return tibbles (previously returned plain lists columns). longer replace negative corrected values 1. average() .group_by now returns group labels first column. biweight_location() biweight_scale() use unscaled MAD, following standard definition (Beers et al., 1990), biweight_scale()^2 equals biweight_midvariance(). biweight_scale() loses unused tol max_iter arguments. loc = NULL now means “median x”. direct_orthogonal() loses unused max_iter tol arguments, direct_osc() loses max_iter. tol now sets pseudo-inverse tolerance. epo() gains clutter argument (matrix describing external variation). default ncomp now 2, documented. now removes dominant singular directions; , removed smallest ones. o2pls() new interface: o2pls(x, y, ncomp, nx, ny, center, scale). pds() returns transfer_matrix (transfert_matrix), alpha now blends local global models, progress longer printed. projected_osc() always returns corrected training data. New data preprocessed training centers scales. quantile_weight() uses whole-distribution quantiles, Brys et al. (2006), defaults p = 0.125, q = 0.875. summaryStats(robust = TRUE) drops rsd column. applied 1.4826 consistency factor twice, mad already holds correct value. opls() now requires Bioconductor package ropls installed (moved Suggests). longer prints output draws plots. R >= 4.1.0 required.

title: specProc 0.2.0
text: Fixed crashes baseline_arpls(), whittaker(), baseline_lsp() (data frames), correlation(method = "bicor"), directOutlyingness(maxRatio = ), direct_osc(), msc(), multipeakfit(), nas(), o2pls(), osc() ("wold", "fearn"), pds(), peakfit(), projected_osc() yGradientglsw(). glsw() yGradientglsw() squared eigenvalues covariance matrix building filter. msc() regressed wavelength instead spectrum reference. generalized_boxplot() transformed ranks instead data. made g--h estimates meaningless. also failed two tails different numbers outliers. pseudo_voigt() counted area offset twice. biweight_scale() used wrong exponent denominator. also ignored reduced = TRUE. biweight_location() iterate. average() ignore missing values. also read bounds factors unused levels missing group values. normalize(method = "background") rejected data frames bkg. plotSpec() connected spectra single line id given. outlierplot() longer changes user’s random number generator state. iqrMethod() longer changes global options. Missing values longer cause errors.

title: specProc 0.2.0
text: Three vignettes based specLIBS: “Preprocessing LIBS spectra” (baseline, normalization judged replicate RSD intraclass correlation, robust screening shots), “Fitting emission lines” (profile choice, sources uncertainty, identifiability) “Predicting soil clay content LIBS spectra” (compositional log-ratio PLS model nested, repeated cross-validation sample, optimism common shortcuts). plot_fit() draws fitted profiles fine wavelength grid. Functions taking response now accept 1-d arrays, output tapply(). New voigt_profile(): exact Voigt profile, computed C++ Faddeeva function Weideman’s (1994) rational approximation (relative error 1e-10). peak_fit() multipeak_fit() now use profile = "voigt"; pseudo-Voigt approximation available profile = "pseudo_voigt". New data set specLIBS: 400 LIBS spectra (50 soil samples x 8 locations, 7152 channels, 199-822 nm) clay, sand silt content sample. generalized_boxplot() whiskers now end extreme observations within fences, standard boxplots. fences returned lower_fence upper_fence. README rewritten around complete worked example specLIBS.

title: specProc 0.2.0
text: Asymmetric least squares arPLS baselines solved C++ banded Cholesky factorization. cost O(n) per spectrum, scale spectra tens thousands channels. EPO GLSW use Eigen’s divide--conquer SVD never form p x p covariance projection matrices. peakfit() multipeakfit() estimate starting values data wL, wG given. multipeakfit() fits lines simultaneously returns line’s contribution. spectrum fails fit produces warning instead stopping whole batch. orthogonalization functions return centers scales, preprocessing can applied new data. Fewer dependencies: corrr, cowplot, forcats, mt, broom ropls longer imported.
